record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Sharp relative isoperimetric inequality for the cube
record.original_question: Let Q be the unit cube in R^N, N≥2. For 0≤t≤1, define f_N(t) as the infimum of the relative perimeter P(S) over measurable subsets S⊂Q with volume |S|=t, where P(S) counts only boundary inside Q. An explicit formula is known for N=2. Is there a similar formula for f_N(t) when N≥3? In particular, is f_N(t) identically 1 near t=1/2?

evidence.quote: Let Q be the unit cube in RN, N ≥ 2. Given a measurable set S ⊂ Q, denote by 1S the characteristic function of S, by |S| = k1SkL1 the volume of S, and by P(S) the relative perimeter of S, i.e., taking into account only the part of the boundary of S inside Q; in other words P(S) is the total mass of the measure ∇1S.
Open Problem 10.1 ([BreBru]). Is there a formula similar to (10.2) for fN (t) when N ≥ 3? In particular, is it true that fN (t) ≡ 1 near t = 1/2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q=(0,1)^N$ denote the open unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $N\geq 2$. For a measurable set $S\subset Q$, write $\mathbf{1}_S$ for its characteristic function, $|S|=\|\mathbf{1}_S\|_{L^1}$ for its volume, and define the relative perimeter
$$P(S)=\|\nabla\mathbf{1}_S\|(Q),$$
the total variation of the distributional gradient of $\mathbf{1}_S$ measured only inside $Q$ (so that the part of $\partial S$ lying on $\partial Q$ is not counted). For each $t\in[0,1]$ define the isoperimetric profile of the cube
$$f_N(t)=\inf\{P(S): S\subset Q\text{ measurable},\ |S|=t\}.$$
For $N=2$ an explicit formula for $f_2(t)$ is known. 

(a) Find an explicit formula for $f_N(t)$ when $N\geq 3$.

(b) Prove or disprove: there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that $f_N(t)\equiv 1$ for all $t\in[\tfrac12-\varepsilon,\tfrac12+\varepsilon]$ (equivalently, that minimizers of volume near $1/2$ are obtained by slicing the cube by a hyperplane parallel to a face).
artifact.status_search_result: Part (b) — that $f_N(t)\equiv 1$ for $t$ sufficiently close to $1/2$ — was settled affirmatively by F. Glaudo (arXiv:2305.20051, 2023), who proved that any subset of $(0,1)^d$ with volume close enough to $1/2$ has relative perimeter at least 1, confirming the Brezis–Bruckstein conjecture in this regime. An explicit closed-form formula for $f_N(t)$ on the whole interval $[0,1]$ in dimensions $N\geq 3$ does not appear to be known.

status_evidence.title: On the Isoperimetric Profile of the Hypercube
status_evidence.snippet: Glaudo proved that a subset of the hypercube (0,1)^d with volume sufficiently close to 1/2 has (relative) perimeter greater than or equal to 1, settling a conjecture by Brezis and Bruckstein.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture f_N(t) ≡ 1 near t=1/2 has been proven.

status_evidence.title: A sharp relative isoperimetric inequality for the square
status_evidence.snippet: Brezis–Bruckstein establish the explicit formula for the relative isoperimetric profile of the unit square, and pose the analogous problem in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The N=2 case is solved with an explicit formula; the higher-dimensional formula remains open.
